headword: {群雄割拠|ぐんゆうかっきょ}
gloss: rivalry of local warlords; many rivals competing for dominance

definitions.gloss: rivalry of local warlords; many rivals competing for dominance
definitions.explanation: A four-character compound ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}) literally meaning "rival heroes occupying separate territories." Originally described the Warring States period when many feudal lords held their own domains. Now also used figuratively to describe any competitive landscape with many strong contenders.

examples.japanese: {戦国時代|せんごくじだい}は{群雄割拠|ぐんゆうかっきょ}の{時代|じだい}だった。
examples.english: The Warring States period was an era of rival warlords competing for dominance.

examples.japanese: スマートフォン{市場|しじょう}は{群雄割拠|ぐんゆうかっきょ}の{状態|じょうたい}だ。
examples.english: The smartphone market is in a state of fierce competition among many rivals.

examples.japanese: かつては{群雄割拠|ぐんゆうかっきょ}だった{業界|ぎょうかい}も、{今|いま}では{大手|おおて}{数社|すうしゃ}に{集約|しゅうやく}されている。
examples.english: The industry that was once a free-for-all of competing rivals has now consolidated into a few major companies.

notes:
USAGE:
A {四字熟語|よじじゅくご} (four-character compound) used both as a noun and as a する verb ({群雄割拠|ぐんゆうかっきょ}する). The literal historical sense describes the Warring States period, but it is frequently used in modern business and sports contexts to describe competitive fields.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {群雄割拠|ぐんゆうかっきょ}の{時代|じだい} (an era of rival powers)
- {群雄割拠|ぐんゆうかっきょ}の{状態|じょうたい} (a state of multiple rivals competing)
- {群雄割拠|ぐんゆうかっきょ}する (to compete as rival powers)

ETYMOLOGY:
{群雄|ぐんゆう} (many heroes/warlords) + {割拠|かっきょ} (each occupying their own territory).
